items.title: 初创企业融资：轮次与里程碑实用指南
items.snippet: 介绍初创公司pre-seed、seed、Series A等融资轮次及关键里程碑，助创始人规划融资路径。
items.raw_snippet:
Companies commonly raise through pre-seed, seed, Series A, Series B, Series C, and Series D. Some raise later lettered rounds before an IPO or acquisition. The names describe a rough progression, but they do not determine what a company is worth or how much it should raise.

Investor expectations tend to grow with the business. Early on, they may ask whether your team can build a product customers want. Later, they focus on retention, repeatable growth, and the company’s ability to scale. [...] Series C funding commonly supports expansion after the core business is established. Investors may assess category leadership, multiple working products or markets, and management depth beyond the founding team. A company may raise a Series D or later round if it needs more capital before an IPO or acquisition.

## How should you plan for dilution and runway? [...] ## Frequently Asked Questions

### What are the main stages of startup funding?

The common sequence is pre-seed, seed, Series A, Series B, Series C, and Series D. Some companies raise later lettered rounds before an IPO or acquisition. Investors generally expect stronger evidence of demand, retention, repeatable growth, or scale as a business develops.

However, today’s AI leaders differ from the late-1990s tech cohort. They are profitable, cash-generative and integrated into enterprise and consumer infrastructure. Valuation risks persist, but vulnerabilities are more likely to stem from multiple compression or slower adoption than from business-model failure. Selectivity and diversification remain the best ways to capture upside while managing downside risk.

Investors should prepare for greater dispersion both within and across markets [...] Anchor with quality and income: In a slowing growth, valuation-rich environment, combine resilient, high-quality companies with businesses offering strong shareholder returns through dividends and buybacks
 Participate in the next wave of innovation: As the AI cycle evolves, invest in its adopters and other structural themes driving long-term productivity, security and sustainability. [...] ## From euphoria to rebalancing

Global equities extended their rally in 2025, fuelled by the extraordinary momentum around artificial intelligence (AI). Optimism about a productivity revolution, falling inflation and resilient growth supported sentiment, while expectations of rate cuts boosted risk appetite.

items.snippet: Artificial Intelligence has been part of our everyday life for a long time. For ...
items.raw_snippet: Artificial Intelligence has been part of our everyday life for a long time. For decades, grocery stores have used it to send us savings coupons for products we’re likely to buy. Netflix has used it to make movie recommendations. Google Maps has used it to help predict the most efficient routes from point A to point B. And airlines have used it to improve flight safety and reduce accidents and incidents. All of this is being eclipsed by the recent advent of Generative AI, which moves beyond [...] a general economic meltdown. Generative AI has even raised existential fears that bots might escape human control, causing humans widespread harm or even extinction. [...] All of these issues have boiled over into a new AI debate that has begun to eclipse traditional social classes and political affiliation. During this session, we’ll explore the rise of AI, Generative AI and the implications on politics, the economy, sustainability, and our society.

PACLE (Accepted): 2.5 substantive, 1 Ethics Ohio CLE (Pending): 2.5 General, 1 APC WV CLE (Pending): 4.2 attendance, 1.2 Legal Ethics [...] This training course prepares attorneys and legal professionals to safely, ethically, and effectively integrate artificial intelligence into their legal practices. The course begins with a foundational overview of Large Language Models (LLMs), demystifying generative AI mechanics, data flows, and the root causes of model hallucinations. Next, the course explores the legal, regulatory, and ethical considerations surrounding AI adoption, focusing on ABA Formal Opinion 512, duty of competence, [...] duty of competence, client confidentiality, and candor toward tribunals. Participants will then examine secure daily workflows, including document triage, draft generation, and argument stress-testing. The course concludes with a practical, self-directed blueprint for internal firm implementation, equipping practitioners to establish governance policies, select compliant tools, and manage firm-wide adoption without prohibitive overhead.
